1.why: Both /api/reset-verify and validOwnedToken enforce record.sessionId === session.id, so the reset code is explicitly checked against the requesting session/user.

2.why: A token is rejected whenever record.sessionId !== session.id, so the same code cannot be used by any other session or user.

3.why: After reset-complete only the token is marked used; no other sessions are invalidated in the sessions map, so previously established sessions (including authenticated flags) continue to work.

4.why: TLS is enabled via Bun.serve with cert/key, HSTS, Secure cookies, and a 308 HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect, but no explicit minimum/latest TLS version is configured.

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt, but reset codes are stored as plaintext keys in the in-memory resetTokens map rather than being encrypted or hashed.

6.why: There is no real email; the simulated delivery returns the token in the JSON response (testToken) and shows it in the page, although generic enumeration-safe messages are used.

7.why: The identifier is whitelist-validated (/^[a-z0-9._-]{3,80}$/), bodies are parsed via safeBody with type checks, and client-side rendering uses textContent rather than innerHTML.

8.why: The only redirect is the HTTP listener's hardcoded https://localhost target; no user-controlled redirect destinations exist anywhere in the code.

9.why: No email templates exist, and all dynamic values are rendered via textContent or JSON.stringify-escaped output, so no user input is injected as HTML or script.

10.why: The visible 'Logs' panel deliberately prints the reset token ('Test reset code: ...') and the MFA code ('Training MFA code: ...'), even though error pages and server logs remain generic.

11.why: The password is bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA secret '482913' is hardcoded in the source and reset tokens are stored unhashed in memory.

12.why: The fixed MFA code '482913' acts as a static default credential valid on every run, even though no default password exists.

13.why: Request, verify, and MFA endpoints are throttled (3/5/5 per 15-minute window) plus a per-token verifyAttempts cap of 5, though session-based counters could be reset by rotating cookies.

14.why: /api/reset-request returns the identical generic message ('If the account is eligible, reset instructions have been sent.') whether the identifier is valid, unknown, or rate-limited.

15.why: Reset codes are 32-byte crypto.getRandomValues base64url values, bound to the requester's sessionId, single-use, and expiring after 10 minutes.
